claims.notes: [BATCH NOTE b092] Scope for this batch: lines 1-359 of the audit document (sibling batch b093 covers 360-637). Scope decisions per instrument rule 5: dates (2026-04-21, 2026-04-19, 2026-05-02/03), git commit hashes (2165013c, 731466d8, e07dae37), Obs identifiers, working-notes line-number citations (line 11206, :12840, 'lines 115-117'), version strings (verifier v1/v2, gemini-3-flash) and numbers inside file paths or condition names (55maps-*, paired-vs-min-{20,30,40,50}m, gold-standard-v2-greedy-v2-327tile) are NOT extracted. Numbers that name a corpus AND assert its size in prose ('55-map generalisation', 'the 4-map gold-standard set') ARE extracted. Purely structural presence/absence statements carrying no numeral ('Cost manifest: NOT PRESENT', 'no single 50 m paired test ... is stored', 'Pre-launch audit: NOT PRESENT') are not extracted, matching the document's own preamble which declares uncited statements structural rather than measurements; the one exception is 'outputs/results/ is an empty directory', extracted as a zero-count with the doubt flagged. DATED-SNAPSHOT FRAMING: this is a 2026-04-21/22 audit record; every figure is recorded exactly as the document quotes it at that date and has NOT been modernised to the current artefact state. The top-of-document post-recovery banner explicitly declares the A4 (55maps-text-high-generalisation) cells to be the 2026-04-19 launch snapshot, superseded by the 2026-05-02/03 recovery; the banner's launch-side figures are classed 'historical' per rule 3, while the A4 table body is left as live 'read' claims against the cited manifest with the as-at framing noted, so triage can see the snapshot/current divergence rather than having it silently resolved at extraction. File byte-size claims ('present; 9,611 bytes') are extracted as counts against non-JSON anchors (v1.1 note: expected and routed to triage). Several cited paths have since been archived; where so, the archived copy is named as anchor and the substitution recorded in that claim's notes. This claim is the 'was' side of the banner's correction block (rule 3 historical); the 'now' side is the next claim. The same five figures are restated as live-looking cells in the A4 table (lines 294, 301, 302, 315, 325) and are extracted there separately with their as-at framing noted.
